q-117146.name: Question 1
q-117146.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/8f818ebe4aea90c33ba1eb3feccf988b0486565da9177df1e98460a950f8b22e.png)

In the figure above, $\overset{\to }{OC}$ is the bisector of $∠AOB.$ If $m∠AOB={58}^{∘}$, find $m∠AOC.$
q-117146.worked_solution:
The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Each of these congruent angles has a measure that is half the measure of the larger bisected angle. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AOC & =\frac{m∠AOB}{2} \\  & =\frac{{58}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={29}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

In the figure above, OC→ is the bisector of ∠AOB. If m∠AOB=58∘, find m∠AOC.

a
27∘
b
29∘
c
30∘
d
24∘
e
25∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Each of these congruent angles has a measure that is half the measure of the larger bisected angle. So, we have

m∠AOC=m∠AOB2=58∘2=29∘.

q-117143.name: Question 2
q-117143.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/6239a47a2bd88b631f9058c7afe3b59c10b8e71fb8957fe7a354cc7e72daf69d.png)

In the figure above, $m∠BOC={72}^{∘}$ and $m∠AOC=7x+{9}^{∘}.$ If $\overset{\to }{OC}$ is the bisector of $∠AOB,$ find the value of $x.$
q-117143.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/6a49c1d69a34d0159cd24869b51cb7a517021a147e0e831b969c1135f6b533fc.png)

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Thus, $∠AOC≅∠BOC.$ Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AOC & =m∠BOC \\ 7x+{9}^{∘} & ={72}^{∘} \\ 7x & ={63}^{∘} \\ x & ={9}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

q-173763.name: Question 3
q-173763.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/5291d267ce1e895cfe75261a36c9dbc660a32935b6858ec8986379ee8c8bb766.png)

Since the angles $∠BOD$ and $∠DOA$ are supplementary, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOD & ={180}^{∘}-m∠DOA \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{84}^{∘} \\  & ={96}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COD & =\frac{m∠BOD}{2} \\  & =\frac{{96}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={48}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COA & =m∠COD+m∠DOA \\  & ={48}^{∘}+{84}^{∘} \\  & ={132}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

132
∘.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the angles ∠BOD and ∠DOA are supplementary, we have

m∠BOD=180∘−m∠DOA=180∘−84∘=96∘.

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get m∠COD=m∠BOD2=96∘2=48∘.

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have m∠COA=m∠COD+m∠DOA=48∘+84∘=132∘.

In the figure above, $∠BOA$ is a straight angle,  and $\overset{\to }{OC}$ is the bisector of $∠BOD.$ If $m∠DOA={134}^{∘},$ find $m∠COA.$
q-76634.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/8dfbfa4aaa55e2f8175fe829fccc945d29733a84fc5c1641f099b09d805ada2b.png)

Since the angles $∠BOD$ and $∠DOA$ are supplementary, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOD & ={180}^{∘}-m∠DOA \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{134}^{∘} \\  & ={46}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COD & =\frac{m∠BOD}{2} \\  & =\frac{{46}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={23}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COA & =m∠COD+m∠DOA \\  & ={23}^{∘}+{134}^{∘} \\  & ={157}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-76640.html:
Question 5
?

In the figure above, OD→ is the bisector of ∠AOC. If m∠BOA=131∘ and m∠BOC=73∘, find m∠DOA.

a
25∘
b
29∘
c
32∘
d
35∘
e
27∘
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the angle addition postulate, we have

m∠COA=m∠BOA−m∠BOC=131∘−73∘=58∘.

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, m∠DOA=m∠COA2=58∘2=29∘.

q-117261.problem:

In the figure above, $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠COA.$ If $m∠BOA={127}^{∘}$ and $m∠BOD={75}^{∘},$ find $m∠BOC.$
q-117261.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/72c0047a8d0b513a5159d31addf0e4c0c2eeefe0e73ceeadf8e154c37f583039.png)

By the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DOA & =m∠BOA-m∠BOD \\  & ={127}^{∘}-{75}^{∘} \\  & ={52}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, 

$$
m∠DOA=m∠COD={52}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC & =m∠BOD-m∠COD \\  & ={75}^{∘}-{52}^{∘} \\  & ={23}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-52777.name: Question 7
q-52777.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/7bd5be67491f109f8041d33768aca872f9dc7242dd1d91bcbfe116a8277f5bf1.png)

In the diagram above $∠BOA$ is a straight angle. Given that $\overset{\to }{OD}$ and $\overset{\to }{OE}$ are the bisectors of $∠COA$ and $∠BOC$, respectively, find $m∠EOD.$
q-52777.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/19334b594e8567464103bacc4f0978cbbbc664c3cc5a1a6edd5789e822030c4b.png)

Let $m∠COD=x$ and $m∠EOC=y.$ Then,

$$
m∠EOD=m∠COD+m∠EOC=x+y.
$$

Since $\overset{⟶}{OD}$ is a bisector of $∠COA,$ we have

$$
m∠COA=2x.
$$

Since $\overset{⟶}{OE}$ is a bisector of $∠BOC,$ we have

$$
m∠BOC=2y.
$$

Finally, since $∠AOB$ is a straight angle, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COA+m∠BOC & =m∠AOB \\ 2x+2y & ={180}^{∘} \\ x+y & ={90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $m∠EOD=x+y={90}^{∘}.$

a

q-76644.name: Question 8
q-76644.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/fb5fddbf843a89ffbefeaed1976a2bfd159fea9a41665f99aee260f110016e1c.png)

In the figure above, $\overset{\to }{OD}$ and $\overset{\to }{OE}$ are the bisectors of $∠AOC$ and $∠BOC,$ respectively. If $m∠DOC=x,$ $m∠COE=2x+{2}^{∘},$ and $m∠AOB={130}^{∘},$ find the value of $m∠BOC.$
q-76644.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191213/assets/484a70ad0c9eeca1ea03db65f5c687074189ac93f9894b64598278dc285d0d83.png)

First, let's express the measures of $∠AOC$ and $∠BOC,$ in terms of $x.$

Since $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠AOC,$ we have

$$
m∠AOC=2m∠DOC=2x.
$$

Since $\overset{\to }{OE}$ is the bisector of $∠BOC,$ we have

$$
m∠BOC=2m∠COE=4x+{4}^{∘}.
$$

Since $m∠AOB={130}^{∘},$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AOC+m∠BOC & =m∠AOB \\ 2x+4x+{4}^{∘} & ={130}^{∘} \\ 6x+{4}^{∘} & ={130}^{∘} \\ 6x & ={126}^{∘} \\ x & ={21}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We are asked to find $m∠BOC.$ Substituting $x={21}^{∘}$ into the expression for $m∠BOC$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC & =4({21}^{∘})+{4}^{∘} \\  & ={84}^{∘}+{4}^{∘} \\  & ={88}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
